newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge up to new record, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge up to new record, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted minor gains in subdued trade on Monday although profit-taking erased part of the early gains, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed at a sixth consequtive all-time high of 92,134.21, up 375.30 points, or 0.41 percent from Friday's previous record of 91,758.91, but down from a day's high of 92,896. It had surged 5.49 percent last week.
Trade volume plunged to 18.54 trillion lira ($180.9 million) from Friday's record 35.89 trillion ($352.6 million).
In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.9, unchanged from Friday and compared to a record of $1 on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
"The index's drop was prevented by buying in bluechip Eregli and a few other utilities. But activity mostly focused on minor shares today," said Haldun Sertel from Can securities.
"However, I don't think the market can keep these gains in coming days if there is no fresh cash entry," he added.
